name: Sudan Archives
label: Stones Throw
lede: Brittney Parks left a pop duo her stepfather had planned, taught herself beats on an iPad, and taught the violin to share a stage with a drum machine. Pitchfork has put her on its year-end list three times.

eras.title: Kicked out of the pop duo
eras.text: Parks grows up in Cincinnati playing violin by ear, skips the pop-duo career her stepfather had lined up, and lands in Los Angeles at 19 with a violin and an iPad.

years.h: Sudan Archives gets its name from Sudanese fiddlers
years.p: Brittney Parks, a Cincinnati violinist raised on Irish folk tunes, takes the name at 17 from the Sudanese fiddling she'd been studying, Stereogum reports.
years.xp:
Parks started violin in fourth grade and learned by ear. Stereogum says she named herself Sudan around 17, after falling for Sudanese fiddlers; she cites Asim Gorashi and the Cameroonian electronic pioneer [[Francis Bebey|fab6adab-b46f-45f8-8700-bc44408ba583]] as touchstones.

It became a line she repeats in interviews: the violin is a Black instrument, and Western classical training doesn't tell you that.

years.src: NPR: I'm different · Wikipedia: Sudan Archives
years.h: Her stepfather, a LaFace Records man, books her into a pop duo
years.p: N2 was to be Parks and her twin sister Cat. She skipped rehearsals to go to electronic shows.
years.xp:
NPR reports her stepfather helped launch LaFace Records, home to OutKast and TLC, and tried to shape the sisters into N2. Parks pushed back: "I just wanna make my own s***," she told NPR.

She was kicked out at 19, NPR says, and moved to Los Angeles.

years.src: NPR: I'm different · Stereogum: The Story Behind
years.h: Ethnomusicology at Pasadena City College by day, Low End Theory by night
years.p: She makes beats on an iPad, then an MPC, in Los Angeles.
years.xp: At Low End Theory, the Los Angeles beat scene's weekly club night, Parks met people from Stones Throw, NPR reports. Stereogum credits the label's [[Matthewdavid|a9549228-8e49-41d2-9a04-0b5ea2056800]] with discovering her.

eras.title: Stones Throw, a violin and a loop pedal
eras.text: Two EPs on Stones Throw, then a debut album that made her a year-end fixture.

years.h: Her debut EP, Sudan Archives, comes out on Stones Throw
years.p: Violin, loops and beats: the first of two EPs before her first album.

years.cap: Sudan Archives at Codfish Hollow, Maquoketa, Iowa, August 29, 2018
years.src: Wikipedia: Sudan Archives · NPR: I'm different
yt: Nont For Sale, live on KEXP
years.h: "Nont for Sale", from the Sink EP, becomes a Stereogum favorite
years.p: Stereogum named the song a favorite of May 2018, and she played it live on KEXP.
years.xp:
Sink was the second of the two EPs Stones Throw released before her debut album, per NPR. NPR's 2018 profile described her sound as pulling from everywhere.

By the time Athena arrived she was calling the EPs short forms: "I kinda consider those EPs haikus and now they're full stories," she told NPR.

years.cap: Sudan Archives at Codfish Hollow, Maquoketa, Iowa
years.src: Wikipedia: Athena · Stereogum: The Story Behind · NPR: I'm different
years.h: She couldn't find a Black Athena, so Athena became her autobiography
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 7.7, and the New York Times ranked it No. 4 of 2019.
years.xp:
Parks produced it with help from [[Washed Out|74a30f2a-dae6-4e99-8a75-cb0f93b31aa6]], [[Paul White|1e6ee12a-b6dd-4557-99a3-17261bc510f8]] and Will Archer, per Wikipedia. Metacritic scores it 83.

She has said she wanted a Black female goddess because she didn't see any in pictures of Athena. Stereogum calls the record her autobiography; NPR quotes her describing it as the biography of life from 19 to now.

eras.title: The basement studio
eras.text: Lockdown, a home studio and full creative control make the record that lands her at No. 2 on Pitchfork's 2022 list.

years.h: Her Tiny Desk Concert strips Athena down to violin and voice
years.p: NPR published the set on June 29, 2020.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the Tiny Desk concert in 2020, and WXPN covered the June release.

years.cap: Sudan Archives at Mississippi Studios, Portland, September 29, 2022
years.h: Pitchfork names "Home Maker" a Best New Track
years.p: The lead single from the record she built in her basement.

years.big: Everybody had to give me everything, and I was the person overseeing all of the ideas.
q: Everybody had to give me everything, and I was the person overseeing all of the ideas.
years.src: Wikipedia: Natural Brown Prom Queen · Rolling Stone
years.h: Natural Brown Prom Queen lands at No. 2 on Pitchfork's 2022 list
years.p: Pitchfork scored it 9.0, and the New York Times had it No. 4.
years.xp:
Parks says she built the studio in her Los Angeles basement during lockdown with then-partner James McCall (Nocando, All City Jimmy). She originally called the record Homesick, missing Cincinnati and her mother; the title refers to a prom she missed. Closer "#513" is her area code, with producer [[Hi-Tek|fcb6d9df-6cef-4f33-8850-7570bcc99718]].

Collaborators sent stems and she assembled the record herself, Rolling Stone reports.

years.cap: Sudan Archives at her Austin City Limits taping
years.h: "Selfish Soul" makes her network TV debut on Late Show
years.p: The video is one of her most-watched, and she later played the song on Austin City Limits.

eras.title: Gadget Girl
eras.text: Awards, a breakup, a house sale, and a dance record where club engineering shares the stage with the violin.

years.cap: Sudan Archives at ACL Live during SXSW, Austin, March 17, 2023
years.h: Two Libera Awards go to Natural Brown Prom Queen
years.p: Best Breakthrough Artist/Release and Best R&B Record, handed out by the independent-music industry itself.

years.h: "Dead" arrives months after a breakup and a house sale
years.p: The first single from The BPM, an album Parks made through a breakup, a home sale and, in NME's words, major upheaval.
years.xp: NME says Parks made the album after a breakup, a home sale and major upheaval, and calls it cathartic. Wikipedia notes she and McCall separated during its production.

years.cap: Sudan Archives at the Fonda Theatre, Hollywood
years.src: Wikipedia: The BPM · Album of the Year · NPR: In an era · NME · Pitchfork: The 50 Best Albums of 2025
years.h: The BPM goes to the club, with a cyborg on the cover
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.4 and ranked it No. 13 of 2025.
years.xp:
Stones Throw released it as her third album. Parks drew on her parents' Michigan and Illinois roots, recorded in both cities, and introduced an alter ego, Gadget Girl. Wikipedia lists Metacritic at 83; Album of the Year shows an 81 critic average.

NPR describes a grief-stricken woman meeting her digital avatar. Parks told NME the violin is very Black and that movement has become part of her self-care. One critic noted the concept pushes her violin to the back.

years.h: She builds a "violin guitar" for the road
years.p: The custom instrument anchors the live show, with North American dates running through January and February 2026.
years.xp: NME mentions the custom instrument and a family collaboration with her twin sister and a cousin. Wikipedia lists the tour dates.
